newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds Germany late to enact EU rules on waste water.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Germany late to enact EU rules on waste water.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday Germany failed to implement the Council directive on waste water treatment within the prescribed time limit.
Germany told the court it was currently in the process of preparing the measures needed to transpose the directive.
The court said member states may not plead provisions, practices or circumstances existing in an internal legal system to justify lateness in adopting directives.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Failure of a member state to fulfil its obligations - Directive 91/271/EEC - Urban waste water treatment"
Commission of the European Communities, applicant

application for a declaration that, by not adopting the laws, regulations or administrative provisions necessary to comply with Council directive 91/271/EEC of 21 May 1991 concerning urban waste water treatment (OJ 1991 L 135, p. 40) or, in any event, by not notifying the Commission thereof, the Federal Republic of Germany has failed to fulfil its obligations under that directive and under the EC Treaty

1. Declares that, by not adopting the laws, regulations or administrative provisions necessary to comply with Council directive 91/271/EEC of 21 May 1991 concerning urban waste water treatment the Federal Republic of Germany has failed to fulfil its obligations under that directive and under the EC Treaty
2. Orders the Federal Republic of Germany to pay the costs.
